query: What visit reasons point to different departments?

per_column.name: primary_clinical_domain
per_column.rationale: Clinical domains (cardiovascular, dermatology, orthopedic, neurological) are essentially aliases of hospital departments. Predicting department from clinical domain is near-tautological restatement of the target.

per_column.name: presenting_problem_category
per_column.rationale: Chronic management vs acute illness vs trauma vs mental health is a functional characterization of the visit that correlates with department but does not directly name it; a legitimate, non-deterministic signal.

per_column.name: body_system
per_column.rationale: Body system (cardiac, skin, musculoskeletal, neurological) maps almost one-to-one onto specialty departments, making it a restatement of the focus rather than an independent predictor.

per_column.name: visit_acuity_level
per_column.rationale: Acuity (routine/urgent/life-threatening) is orthogonal to which organ-system department; it carries some signal (e.g., emergency vs preventive) without encoding the department itself.

per_column.name: symptom_onset_pattern
per_column.rationale: Onset pattern (sudden vs chronic vs asymptomatic) is a genuine descriptive feature of the complaint, correlated with but not determinative of department.

per_column.name: encounter_type
per_column.rationale: Encounter type (acute unscheduled, scheduled followup, well visit, emergency triage) describes visit logistics; predictive of department distribution without restating it.

per_column.name: care_phase
per_column.rationale: Care phase (new diagnosis, active treatment, surveillance, prevention) is a process feature that plausibly correlates with department mix and is not a component of the target.

per_column.name: chronic_vs_acute
per_column.rationale: Chronicity classification is a legitimate independent feature; largely redundant with presenting_problem_category but not a restatement of department.

per_column.name: procedure_performed
per_column.rationale: The procedure performed is known only during/after the encounter (post-outcome), and procedure type (surgical, biopsy, device implant) strongly encodes department, constituting leakage.

per_column.name: specialist_referral_needed
per_column.rationale: Referral to a subspecialty/surgical service is determined at/after the visit and directly implies destination department; post-outcome and target-revealing.

judge.rationale: Several columns (primary_clinical_domain, body_system) are near-aliases of the department target and are restatements/leakage, while procedure_performed and specialist_referral_needed are post-encounter variables that leak the outcome. The remaining features (presenting_problem_category, visit_acuity_level, symptom_onset_pattern, encounter_type, care_phase, chronic_vs_acute) are legitimate pre-outcome descriptors, but they cluster on the acute/chronic and acuity axes and are heavily mutually redundant, so their combined incremental predictive leverage over the existing urgency and reason_for_visit columns is moderate rather than strong.
